text: Kenji left home with one tea bowl, to sell in the city.
His grandmother had made it. It was plain, and a little crooked.
At the river, the rain caught an old ferryman. Kenji poured him tea.
On the mountain pass, the snow caught an old woman. Kenji poured her tea.
At the festival, a little girl was lost. Kenji poured her tea.
In the city, a rich man offered him ten gold coins.
Kenji thought of the rain, the snow, and the lanterns.
So he carried the bowl home, and poured the first cup for her.
Some things are worth more full than sold.
